Found the bug. The changelog claims "Ignore dunder attributes when creating Tokens (issue672)" but the actual fix is missing from `_TokenType.__getattr__` in sqlparse/tokens.py. Because `__getattr__` doesn't skip dunder names, any dunder lookup (e.g. `__deepcopy__`, `__copy__`, `__reduce__`, `__reduce_ex__`, `__getstate__`, `__setstate__` used by `copy.deepcopy`/`copy.copy`) creates a new `_TokenType` instance instead of raising `AttributeError`. CHANGELOG:152: * Ignore dunder attributes when creating Tokens (issue672).

Found the bug. The changelog claims "Ignore dunder attributes when creating Tokens (issue672)" but the actual fix is missing from `_TokenType.__getattr__` in sqlparse/tokens.py. Because `__getattr__` doesn't skip dunder names, any dunder lookup (e.g. `__deepcopy__`, `__copy__`, `__reduce__`, `__reduce_ex__`, `__getstate__`, `__setstate__` used by `copy.deepcopy`/`copy.copy`) creates a new `_TokenType` instance instead of raising `AttributeError`. Python then tries to call that returned `_TokenType` object as if it were the dunder method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported regression for 'copy issue672'.

Fix: make `__getattr__` raise `AttributeError` for dunder-style names so the normal Python protocol (e.g. copy/pickle falling back to default behavior) works correctly again, restoring the intended issue672 fix.
